summary: [spec-fidelity] Two rewritten scenarios say what the bound test and the binary contradict. report.dashboard.14 now says the 409 BRIEF_PAGE_STALE carries 'an error.details entry for the edited brief'; its test asserts `doc["error"].get("details").is_none()` ('one stale brief is the refusal itself, with no per-id entries'), which is the right behaviour (details is for several causes). Fix the scenario: one refused id answers its own code with no details. skills.install.55 now says each refusal is 'CONFIG_INVALID with the reason SKILLS, or SKILLS_ARGUMENT_INVALID for an unknown provider', but its Given is a canon.yaml that names the unknown provider and the commands run with no --providers: that is CONFIG_INVALID/SKILLS (the test asserts CONFIG_INVALID; I ran it: `skills.providers names bogus` is CONFIG_INVALID reason SKILLS). SKILLS_ARGUMENT_INVALID is the --providers flag; the test only asserts exit 2 for `--providers gemini`. Say which input gives which code and assert the code and the reason SKILLS in the test. Both scenarios are left unsigned.
